site.name: Aztec Mine
site.location: Sugarloaf area, Boulder County Tungsten Mining District
overview: Aztec Mine is a historic underground tungsten mine in Boulder County's tungsten-mining district near Sugarloaf.
Federal mineral-record data classify the property as a past tungsten producer, while historic Boulder-area mapping preserves the Aztec name among the Sugar Loaf district's mine claims.

timeline.text: The Aztec property was developed as an underground tungsten mine in the Boulder County tungsten district.
A historic Boulder Hydro-Electric Company pipeline-alignment map preserved by the Carnegie Library for Local History labels the Aztec mine among Sugar Loaf Mining District claims.
U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 245 documented the geology and ore deposits of the Boulder County tungsten district, the regional setting in which the Aztec Mine is recorded.

moreHistory: USGS-derived mineral inventory data identify Aztec as a tungsten mine with underground workings and past production in Boulder County.

The historic pipeline-alignment map places Aztec in the Sugar Loaf mining landscape alongside other named mines and claims, providing independent archival confirmation that the Aztec name was attached to a specific Boulder County mining property.

The mapped mine point near 40.002764, -105.3805493 is a historic site-level reference. It should not be interpreted as a surveyed surviving shaft collar, property boundary, or statement of present-day access.
